name: chaosrat

scripts.coverage:summary: vitest run --coverage --coverage.reportOnFailure --coverage.reporter=text --coverage.reporter=html --coverage.reporter=json-summary && node -e "const c = require('./coverage/coverage-summary.json').total; const f = (n) => n.toFixed(2); console.log('Coverage: ' + f(c.statements.pct) + '% stmts | ' + f(c.branches.pct) + '% branch | ' + f(c.functions.pct) + '% funcs | ' + f(c.lines.pct) + '% lines');"

//: socket.io-client is pinned to exactly 2.0.3 in dependencies and must not be
upgraded. The CHZZK (치지직) Open API session socket speaks Engine.IO
protocol v3 only, verified empirically rather than taken from docs: a
polling handshake against https://ssio01.nchat.naver.com/socket.io/ returns
v3 framing (byte prefix 00 01 01 03 ff, then 0{"sid":...}) for EIO=3, for
EIO=4, and with the EIO parameter omitted entirely -- the server ignores
the protocol-version parameter and always answers with v3 framing. An
Engine.IO v4 server would instead reject EIO=3 with
{"code":5,"message":"Unsupported protocol version"} and answer EIO=4 with
unframed 0{"sid":...}. socket.io-client 3.x/4.x send EIO=4 and parse with
engine.io-parser v5, so they cannot read a v3 frame and fail the
handshake; v3 and v4 also invert the ping direction. Naver's own docs say
'Socket.IO-client 1.0.0 through 2.0.3', but 2.0.3 was simply the newest
release when that sentence was written (2017-06-12, superseded by 2.0.4
four months later) and the whole 2.x line through 2.5.0 speaks Engine.IO
v3 -- this project deliberately stays on the documented 2.0.3 rather than
relying on that wider fact.
parseuri (a transitive dependency reached through socket.io-client 2.x)
is left vulnerable to GHSA-6fx8-h7jm-663j / CVE-2024-36751, a moderate
ReDoS, as an accepted risk rather than an oversight. The advisory itself
lists no patched version: parseuri@0.0.6 is byte-identical to 0.0.5 (same
regex, so not a fix), and parseuri@3.0.2 is ESM-only
("type": "module", exports: "./src/index.js") and cannot be require()'d by
CommonJS socket.io-client 2.x. The only string that ever reaches it is
the session URL returned by CHZZK's own API over HTTPS
(/api/chzzk/session/open), parsed once per connect -- not
attacker-controlled -- and the advisory's CVSS 4.0 vector is
availability-only (VC:N/VI:N/VA:L). This also keeps engine.io-client and
socket.io-client flagged in npm audit by inheritance, so npm audit
reporting 3 moderate findings is the intended steady state, not a
regression to chase.
Rule for the overrides block below: an entry exists only where the
parent package's declared range contains no patched version at all, so
an ordinary npm update cannot reach one. brace-expansion is forced
because every consuming minimatch (9.0.9, 5.1.9) declares ^2.0.x, and
the newest 2.x (2.1.2) is still inside the advisory's <=5.0.7 affected
range -- only a major-crossing override fixes it. socket.io-parser is
forced because socket.io-client@2.0.3 declares ~3.1.1, and every 3.1.x
is vulnerable. engine.io-client's nested ws/xmlhttprequest-ssl overrides
are forced because engine.io-client@3.1.6 declares ws: ~3.3.1 and
xmlhttprequest-ssl: ~1.5.4, and both ranges are entirely vulnerable; the
override is nested rather than global because ws is also resolved by
happy-dom and tmi.js at 8.21.1, and a global entry would downgrade
those. axios, js-yaml and flatted were deliberately NOT given override
entries: their patched versions (axios 1.18.1, js-yaml 4.3.0, flatted
3.4.3) are already inside the ranges their parents (youtube-chat,
@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser, flat-cache) declare, so an ordinary
npm update reaches them without an override.
